name: Laurisilva of Madeira
description: On the Portuguese island of Madeira in the Atlantic, this misty evergreen forest is the largest surviving stretch of laurel forest, a type that once blanketed much of southern Europe. Around 90 percent of it is believed to be untouched primary forest. Its dense, moss-draped canopy shelters many species found nowhere else, including the Madeiran long-toed pigeon.
